newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada panel recommends limited cod fishing.
newsitem.headline: Canada panel recommends limited cod fishing.

text.p: A Canadian government-appointed scientific panel on Thursday recommended a limited re-opening of the cod fishery off Canada's Atlantic coast, which has been closed to commercial fishing since 1993.

The Fisheries Resource Conservation Council, which reports to Canada's Fisheries Minister Fred Mifflin, proposed the opening of a small commercial cod fishery in 1997. The non-binding recommendations include the opening of three fishing zones in the Gulf of St. Lawrence off the coasts of the provinces of Newfoundland, Nova Scotia and Quebec.

If Mifflin accepts the proposals, fishermen will be allowed to catch 22,000 metric tons of cod next year, far below the 38,000 tonnes taken in those zones in 1993. The minister is expected to make a decision by year end.

The Canadian government banned commercial cod fishing off the country's Atlantic coast in stages in 1992 and 1993 because fish stocks were severely depleted. The shutdown drastically affected the economy in Newfoundland, which has an unemployment rate of 18.6 percent.

"We are including among our recommendations to the minister that we move forward, cautiously and prudently, with low-level re-openings of commercial cod fisheries, with quota recommendations focused on re-building these stocks," Fred Woodman, chairman of the conservation council, told reporters.

Despite the recommendations, the council said it found only minimal improvement in cod stocks along the Grand Banks, a once fertile fishing ground off Newfoundland that was the mainstay of Atlantic Canada's commercial fishery until it was closed in 1992.
"Our offshore survey showed very little improvement, especially in the north, although in southern areas there are enouraging signs," Woodman said.

While the council blamed overfishing and unusually cold water temperatures for the dramatic decline in cod stocks, it also said the slow recovery in fish stocks was being hampered by an explosion in seal populations.
The council recommended continuing the controversial seal hunt along the Atlantic coast and the possible use of contraceptive methods to control the growth of the seal population.
The council estimated that 5 million harp seals live in the waters surrounding Newfoundland and Labrador and that they consume about 140,000 tonnes of cod each year.
